---
title: "WF2 — Analyze projections"
---

`analyze_projections.smk` reduces CMIP6 projections to basin monthly temperature and precipitation change factors. These factors position the stress-test grid against projection space; they do not determine WF3 perturbations.

## Rules

| Rule | Operation |
|---|---|
| `all` (target) | Collect change factors, plots, and records. |
| 2.01 `delineate_region` | Define the shared basin region. |
| 2.02 `delineate_subbasins_and_rivers` | Build shared vectors. |
| 2.03 `fetch_cmip6_projections` | Fetch raw slices for configured model, scenario, member, and variable keys. |
| 2.04 `reduce_to_basin_averages` | Reduce each local slice to a monthly basin series. |
| 2.05 `derive_change_factors` | Compare future and reference windows and write tables and report. |
| 2.05b `prepare_projection_analysis` | Compute analysis-window diagnostic tables and availability. |
| 2.06 `plot_climate_projections` | Render projection figures. |
| 2.07 `gather_benchmarks` | Merge benchmark parts. |
| 2.08 `gather_logs` | Merge log parts. |

The `all` target collects these products. Rule 2.03 is the remote data read; subsequent reduction uses the acquired slices.

## Rule flow

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["2.01–2.02 Region and vectors"] --> C["2.04 Basin monthly series"]
  B["2.03 Fetch CMIP6 slices"] --> C
  C --> D["2.05 Change factors"]
  C --> G["2.05b Analysis tables"]
  G --> E["2.06 Projection figures"]
  D --> F["2.07–2.08 Records"]
  E --> F
  G --> F
```

Fetching fans out by configured model, scenario, member, and variable before monthly reduction.

## Configuration

The project file supplies `project.catalog`, `basin.region`, and `basin.resolution`. Its `workflows.analyze_projections` stanza enables the workflow and points to its YAML file through `config_path`.

The workflow file, `test_case/project_config_rapid_analyze_projections.yml`, sets `catalog` (the CMIP6 catalog), `ensemble` (output namespace), `models` and `scenarios` (the ensemble subset), `members.preference` (member selection order), and `variables` (source mapping, canonical rate or state, units, and relative or absolute change). `reference_window` supplies historical years; each `future_windows` entry supplies years and an output `name`. The template at `config/templates/project_config.analyze_projections.template.yml` also documents optional `members.selection`, `members.overrides`, and `stats`.

```yaml
catalog: config/catalogs/cmip6_data.yml
ensemble: cmip6
models: [NOAA-GFDL/GFDL-ESM4, INM/INM-CM4-8]
scenarios: [ssp245]
members: {preference: [r1i1p1f1]}
variables:
  precip: {source: precip, canonical: rate, units: mm/day, change: relative}
  temp: {source: temp, canonical: state, units: degC, change: absolute}
reference_window: {start: 2000, end: 2014}
future_windows:
  - {start: 2046, end: 2054, name: mid}
```

## Inputs

Inputs are the basin polygon, cataloged CMIP6 data, and the selected model/scenario/member/variable combinations. The reference and future windows define the compared periods. WF2 does not read a scenario collection or model responses.

## Outputs

WF2 retains the acquired slices and basin monthly series, a change-factor product by model, scenario, and horizon, projection figures, and merged logs and benchmarks. Interpret these as plausibility context alongside the response surface, not as forcing for its simulations.

The `analysis/` tables use 30 complete water years around each configured future horizon. The reference is
the last 30 complete configured water years, or the historical fallback (January: WY 1985–2014; October:
WY 1984–2013). These windows are separate from the configured windows of the overlay CSVs. The
`_engine/analysis_record.json` records shifts, historical joins, eligibility, equal-model reductions
and product availability. Seasonal precipitation changes use weighted mean rates; this differs from the lab's
total-based percentages. Precipitation CV uses period integrals. Analysis arithmetic uses float64 inputs;
the aligned change-factor arithmetic retains its existing precision and dry-reference rule.

Rule 2.06 reads only the analysis tables and record. Figures live in `plots/full_period/` and one
`plots/period_<start>_<end>/` folder per distinct analysis window. Availability determines the PNGs:
coverage, annual member overviews and anomaly trajectories, annual/seasonal change and variability
strips, monthly cycles, sign agreement and change-factor clouds. A combined cloud is written only when
at least two distinct windows have paired changes. Missing products carry reasons rather than blank PNGs.

`plots/figure_captions.md` describes every produced figure and lists unavailable and retired products;
`_engine/figure_captions.json` maps ordinary PNG paths to captions and counts. Set
`captioned_figures: true` in the workflow YAML for copies under `plots/captioned/`, recorded by each
manifest entry's `captioned_path`. Spread describes the ensemble, not a confidence interval; sign
counts are diagnostic agreement, not likelihood. The predecessor `plots/overview/` and `plots/windows/`
products are retired. Existing files there are left in place but no longer targeted.
